transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you in to see me?

I’ve been really slow lately. At work, it feels like my hands are moving through glue—just sectioning hair or mixing color takes me forever. People have started noticing I’m not as quick as I used to be.
Along with feeling slowed down, have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Yeah. Most days I wake up with this heavy, flat sadness in my chest. It just feels like… what’s the point in trying to build the life I had planned?
Have you noticed any shaking or trembling in your hands, especially when they are resting?
I haven’t really noticed any shaking in my hands, no.
Have you ever had a period of time lasting a few days or more where you felt unusually energized, on top of the world, or needing much less sleep than usual?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve had a time like that that I can remember.
Have you ever experienced a period of depression like this before in your life?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time it’s felt like this.
Have you noticed feeling unusually sensitive to the cold compared to other people?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed being more sensitive to the cold than other people.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical or neurological conditions?
No, I haven’t been diagnosed with any medical or neurological conditions that I know of.
About how long have you been feeling this sadness and slowness?
It’s been about a year and two months now. It’s felt heavy for most of that time.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities and hobbies you normally used to enjoy?

Yeah. I used to enjoy chatting with my clients, helping the newer stylists, and going hiking with friends. Now I mostly just keep my head down and avoid people. I just don’t really have that spark in me anymore.
During this time, have you had any thoughts of wishing you were dead or thoughts of hurting yourself?
I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but sometimes I think it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up, and nobody had to deal with me anymore.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with key symptoms of a major depressive episode, including persistent depressed mood, prominent anhedonia, psychomotor slowing affecting daily work, and passive suicidal ideation. Symptoms have persisted continuously for about 14 months, causing noticeable functional impairment, with no history of manic or hypomanic episodes and no underlying general medical conditions.
